title: Demand Service Rate Programs: Cut for Arrears at a Ceiling Review
content:
**Term 1.** Where the most recent invoice to fall due has stood past its due day longer than the tier's
suspension period and what the window invoiced less what it received stands above the tier's published
credit limit, a cut of 0.25 is taken off.

**Term 2.** Where the most recent invoice to fall due stands past its due day, two or more invoices fell
due in the window and the payments received in it do not clear what it invoiced, a cut of 0.10 is taken
off.

**Term 3.** In any other case nothing is cut for arrears.

The two program figures the terms turn on, under the Demand Service Rate Programs:

| Program | Suspension period (calendar days past due) | Published credit limit (USD) |
|---|---|---|
| Time & Material Account | 45 | 7500 |
| Priority Response Program | 45 | 15000 |
| Block Hour Service Program | 45 | 25000 |
| Emergency Response Program | 30 | 40000 |
| Critical Facility Response Program | 30 | 75000 |
| Dedicated Technician Program | 30 | 150000 |

| The most recent invoice to fall due | Invoices that fell due in the window | The window's invoiced total less its payments | The cut |
|---|---|---|---|
| past its due day longer than the tier's suspension period | any | above the tier's published credit limit | 0.25 |
| past its due day, by any number of days | two or more, payments not clearing what they invoiced | at or below the tier's published credit limit | 0.10 |
| past its due day, by any number of days | one only | any | nothing is cut |
| not past its due day | any | any | nothing is cut |

**Illustration (hypothetical).** On the Time & Material Account, whose suspension period is 45 calendar
days and whose published credit limit is 7500 US dollars, an account whose most recent invoice stands 50
days past its due day and whose window invoiced 9000 US dollars against 500 US dollars received carries
the cut of 0.25. Where that same account stood 10 days past its due day with three invoices fallen due
in the window and payments short of what they invoiced, the cut would be 0.10.
